results.question: When do I send my first unemployment status report to Kela?
results.answer: In your first application, you report the dates you have been unemployed starting from your first day of unemployment [S1]. To get your first benefit payment, you must file an unemployment status report covering a 2-week period after submitting your first application [S1][S3][S6]. You can only report days of unemployment that have already passed [S1][S3]. If you cannot use the OmaKela e-service, you can send a printed form by post [S2][S5].

results.question: I'm 22 and have no vocational qualification. Do I have to apply for studies to get the benefit?
results.answer: Yes, if you are under 25 and do not have a vocational qualification or higher education degree, you must apply for admission to at least two education programmes that begin in the autumn term [S2][S5][S8]. You must also participate in any entrance exam you are invited to attend [S2][S8]. Contact employment services to agree on the details [S2][S8]. If you do not apply for admission, the KEHA Centre will impose an obligation to work, meaning you cannot get unemployment benefits until you meet certain conditions [S6][S7].

results.question: Can I get my travel costs paid when I go to an aptitude test for labour market training?
results.answer: Yes, as an unemployed jobseeker, you can apply for reimbursement of travel and accommodation expenses from the employment authority when you travel for an aptitude test or admission event for labour market training [S1][S4]. Reimbursement requires that the employment authority considers it appropriate for the availability of labour and your employment [S8].

results.question: Kela paid me labour market subsidy before May 2026. Will they check my income now?
results.answer:
If Kela paid you basic unemployment allowance or labour market subsidy without a means test before you transferred to the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026, Kela will check your income by 30 September 2026 [S2]. This check determines how much income affects your means test [S2]. The means test impacts future payments and is not applied retroactively [S2]. Kela will contact you if necessary and send a separate decision notice if your benefit must be reduced [S2].

Note: The labour market subsidy was abolished when Kela began paying the general social security benefit on 1 May 2026. [S9]

results.question: what is yleistuki
results.answer:
The general social security benefit (*yleistuki*) is a Finnish unemployment benefit intended for unemployed jobseekers who do not qualify for or have used up their earnings-related unemployment allowance [S2][S5]. 

To receive it, you must meet criteria such as being 18–64 years old, living permanently in Finland, being available for work, and registering as an unemployed jobseeker with the employment services [S5][S6]. You must apply for it from Kela [S2][S3]. Earned income and certain benefits reduce the amount, while general housing allowance, child benefit, and social assistance do not [S1][S5][S7].
